record.original_question: Which k-orbit d-polytopes admit a faithful realization in Euclidean d-space E^d as geometrically k-orbit polytopes?

evidence.quote: Problem 32. Which k-orbit d-polytopes have a faithful realization as a geometrically k-orbit polytope in E^d?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be an abstract $d$-polytope, i.e. a ranked partially ordered set with a strict face structure satisfying the usual conditions (existence of a least and greatest face, the diamond condition, and strong flag-connectedness) and whose proper faces have ranks $0,1,\dots,d-1$. The automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts on the set of flags of $\mathcal{P}$; one says that $\mathcal{P}$ is a $k$-orbit polytope if this action has exactly $k$ orbits.

A (Euclidean) realization of $\mathcal{P}$ in $\mathbb{E}^d$ is a mapping $\beta$ that assigns to each vertex of $\mathcal{P}$ a point of $\mathbb{E}^d$, extended recursively to higher-rank faces by assigning to each face $F$ the set (or convex hull, in the convex case) of images of the vertices incident with $F$. The realization is called faithful when $\beta$ is one-to-one on the faces of every rank, so that the geometric figure obtained inherits the combinatorial structure of $\mathcal{P}$ without collapse. The symmetry group $G(\beta(\mathcal{P}))$ is the group of Euclidean isometries of $\mathbb{E}^d$ that permute the realized faces; the realization is called geometrically $k'$-orbit if $G(\beta(\mathcal{P}))$ acts on the flags of $\beta(\mathcal{P})$ with exactly $k'$ orbits.

Characterize the $k$-orbit abstract $d$-polytopes $\mathcal{P}$ that admit a faithful realization in $\mathbb{E}^d$ which is geometrically $k$-orbit, that is, for which the Euclidean symmetry group of the realization acts with exactly the same number $k$ of flag orbits as the combinatorial automorphism group of $\mathcal{P}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a published list of open problems on k-orbit polytopes and is stated as an open question. Searches reveal related results on realizations of abstract regular polytopes and dimension bounds, but no characterization of which k-orbit d-polytopes admit faithful geometrically k-orbit realizations in E^d has been found in the literature.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open problems on k-orbit polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Faithful realization - Polytope Wiki
status_evidence.snippet: If an abstract n-polytope is realized in n-dimensional space such that the geometrical arrangement does not break any rules for traditional polytopes, the realization is said to be faithful.
status_evidence.claim: Standard definition of faithful realization is supported but no characterization for k-orbit polytopes is given.
